batch_strategy: Structure-conditioned response-curve repair with loading contrasts, V2-tail and onset-floor diagnostics, plus four low-similarity transfer anchors.

choices.reason: The m177 1/1 point extends the unusual onset and tail curve below the measured 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 regimes. It tests whether the apparent onset floor and V2 behavior emerge gradually or abruptly; see aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and b514312eda7950cdcf1c.

This lower-loading m177 2/1 point provides a close ratio contrast to the measured aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 and 5442611ea6789d42bc86 rows, while testing whether the very broad V2 prediction is a real tail or loading-sensitive overprediction.

The m177 5/1 point at higher loading bridges the low-ratio candidates and the measured high-ratio rows. It is especially useful for locating the onset-floor transition and separating ratio response from the anomalous V2 tail seen in 4862e2fb71344ce16021.

A m198 2/1 point at intermediate loading fills the local gap between measured 0/1 and 5/1 conditions and contrasts with the recent lower-loading 2/1 result 6f43332e2665523bcccc. It directly teaches ratio-loading interaction near the steep transition.

This m198 10/1 loading contrast tests whether the measured V2 overprediction at 2/1 in 6f43332e2665523bcccc persists at a later ratio, where the measured 50/1 point 0ac58929e586a4da4056 was comparatively well calibrated.

The m141 1/1 point probes the onset before the measured 5/1 and 10/1 responses. It can reveal whether the large V1 underprediction at 5/1 and 20/1, seen in 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and 51f4126a3aadb3239225, begins at weak conditions.

This m141 5/1 lower-loading contrast is directly comparable with the measured higher-loading 5/1 row 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9. It isolates loading effects in a regime where V1 was substantially underpredicted while the tail was less discrepant.

The m204 2/1 higher-loading point extends the measured 2/1 loading series 8cc5dd51f0360e578ac3 and 53c1be5b96937954b9fa toward 150 ul. It tests whether the large loading shift continues into V2 or mainly changes onset.

This lower-loading m204 10/1 point contrasts with the measured high-loading 10/1 response 73502a52708e4f9c2391 and the measured 5/1 rows. It can distinguish a ratio-driven late transition from a loading-driven shift in the broad interval.

The m205 0/1 anchor adds the weak-condition endpoint below the measured 1/1 and 2/1 points 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7 and c973d4c257be9ef08216. It tests where the novel aromatic alcohol scaffold begins its large retention increase.

This m205 1/1 lower-loading point is a matched contrast to the measured 1/1 high-loading row 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7. It helps the model attribute the transfer error to loading rather than to the molecule descriptor alone.

The m205 5/1 higher-loading point extends the measured 5/1 loading sequence 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2 and 48853fd78c77153b963a. It tests whether the observed late response and V2 broadening continue monotonically with loading.

This m216 2/1 midpoint connects the measured weak 0/1 anchor ae187d6f3746213b630c with the late 5/1 and 10/1 responses. It supplies a missing transition point for a molecule with a steep condition curve.
The m216 10/1 higher-loading contrast tests whether the measured 10/1 lower-loading response e47aebe2660b9e1528de is shifted mainly by loading or by the ratio-dependent transition itself.

This m90 5/1 higher-loading point contrasts with the measured lower-loading 5/1 row 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 and the late 10/1 response 96710afeabc594baa359. It directly supervises V2 loading calibration in a large-retention regime.

The m90 1/1 point supplies the low-ratio anchor missing below measured 2/1 and 5/1 conditions. It helps locate the onset transition before the large V1 and V2 values seen in 855832bd4005ac7abdc6 and 96710afeabc594baa359.

This m193 2/1 loading contrast fills the gap between the measured 1/1, 2/1, and 10/1 points and tests whether the V2 underprediction at higher loading, seen in df6457ca86c98c073bf6, begins at lower ratios.

The m193 20/1 higher-loading point contrasts with the measured 20/1 lower-loading row a5f9179bfb146ad70953 and the 10/1 loading response df6457ca86c98c073bf6. It targets separate V2 growth after the onset regime is established.

This m212 1/1 point adds an early-condition anchor below the measured 2/1 and 5/1 rows f6c49d6bc4b677f17278 and d5234e966aa231be05e5. It tests whether the steep response begins before the model's transition region.

The m212 2/1 higher-loading contrast is directly informative against the measured lower-loading 2/1 row f6c49d6bc4b677f17278 and the late measured 10/1 rows 70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73 and 942b8fc9cf013acda52b.

This m178 1/1 point extends the measured 5/1 and 10/1 onset-floor series 17ff889395addf7d6295 and 634f21e11a8442494ce3 toward weak conditions. It helps determine whether V1 and V2 errors begin together.

The m178 2/1 point supplies a second low-ratio anchor between the weak condition and measured 5/1 response. Paired with 17ff889395addf7d6295 and 855456da9ea892f7216b, it discriminates onset-floor failure from tail overprediction.

This m203 1/1 point adds an early anchor below the measured 5/1 and 10/1 responses. It tests whether the strong late-regime overprediction in 04ea307c7b7f3321cc20 is localized to high-ratio conditions.

The m104 10/1 higher-loading point probes the severe high-ratio transfer failure beyond the measured 1/1 anchor 9fa7a350e402312e5860 and the 20/1 row 302e458c5ed2285ca328. It tests whether the apparent retention collapse is molecule-wide or condition-specific.

This m163 5/1 point fills the ratio gap between the measured 1/1 anchor f0d01a802b42b748e6e2 and the much later 50/1 response 4e417c41d918e49abba1. It is a useful structure-condition transfer point for a halogenated aromatic nitrile.

The m163 10/1 point continues the same molecule's PE response before the measured 50/1 condition. Together with f0d01a802b42b748e6e2 and 4e417c41d918e49abba1, it can constrain the transition location and V2 slope.

This m146 5/1 lower-loading point contrasts with the measured 5/1 higher-loading response 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e and the 1/1 anchor 777a87b895af5e6bc380. It targets the strong loading dependence of the high-ratio aromatic heterocycle.

The m146 2/1 higher-loading point fills the lower-ratio segment before measured 5/1 and 10/1 responses. It helps determine whether the large late-ratio error in 9e3ce3497298084abd83 is a transition-location problem or a tail-calibration problem.

This molecule-novel bulky aryl ketone has low similarity to labeled rows and a broad predicted V2 range. It is a transfer anchor for testing whether the structure-conditioned solvent response learned from b1c5816f929ef59f5a87 and 70cba7a21b5a01fb8e73 generalizes beyond familiar scaffolds.

The molecule-novel brominated benzyl alcohol probes a polar HBD-containing scaffold at 10/1 DCM with low structural similarity and substantial predicted V2 width. It tests transfer across halogenation and hydrogen bonding rather than adding another known family point.

This molecule-novel multifunctional carbonyl scaffold targets a late, broad regime with low similarity to observed molecules. Its label can test whether the large-tail behavior seen in b514312eda7950cdcf1c and 0cf0d36290765378ae8d is structural or limited to known families.

The molecule-novel phosphoryl aromatic scaffold is structurally distant from the labeled set and probes a low-ratio DCM condition. It tests whether charged heteroatom interactions require a separate molecule-conditioned solvent response, extending the contrast established by b1c5816f929ef59f5a87.

hypotheses.content: Mobile-phase response is strongly structure-dependent, so nominal PE/EA ratio effects require molecule-conditioned representations, especially for unusual heteroatom or charged scaffolds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A global solvent-strength correction will miscalibrate transition locations across chemical families. Low-similarity anchors can teach the shared representation where those interactions change.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do unusual heteroatom, charge, and hydrogen-bonding environments require distinct ratio-response representations or can they be captured by a common nonlinear surface?

hypotheses.content: V2 calibration is regime-specific: very broad predicted intervals can correspond either to genuine late tails or to severe overprediction, depending on structure, ratio, and loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The V2 head needs direct supervision in both genuine-tail and overbroad-tail regimes. The selected m177, m203, and m104 points provide contrasting labels around these failures.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural and loading features identify genuine V2 broadening before the model extrapolates into the late tail?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume produce learnable shifts within matched molecule-condition families, and the shifts can affect V1, V2, and interval width differently.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts prevent the model from attributing loading shifts to PE/EA or structure. They directly supervise the loading feature and improve shared V1/V2 calibration.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After holding molecule and mobile phase fixed, does loading primarily shift onset, extend the tail, or change both in a family-dependent way?

hypotheses.content: Molecule-novel rows can expose large transfer errors in structure-condition-retention relationships, while novelty alone does not guarantee a large residual.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Overall Row-distribution accuracy requires transfer to scaffolds absent from the current labels. Four low-similarity anchors target distinct polarity, halogenation, carbonyl, and phosphoryl environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which functional-group and interaction changes most often cause transfer failure at otherwise familiar solvent conditions?

hypotheses.content: Several chemical families have steep or threshold-like condition-response curves, so intermediate ratios are more informative than additional unpaired extremes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels constrain local slope and curvature, reducing extrapolation through family-specific transitions and improving both V1 and V2 predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are transition locations shared by chemical family or determined by continuous structural descriptors across families?

hypotheses.content: V1 and V2 errors can decouple: onset may be accurate while the finishing volume is biased, or the reverse.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Acquisition focused only on onset or interval width would leave the other output poorly calibrated. The batch includes V2-focused loading and late-ratio contrasts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structure and loading features predict V2 residuals after conditioning on the onset regime?

hypotheses.content: Onset-floor failures are localized in difficult aromatic ketone and nitroaromatic regimes, where measured V1 remains nonzero while V2 can be either near or far from prediction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Floor-clipped V1 predictions hide meaningful onset differences and distort the shared V1/V2 relationship. Low-ratio m177 and m178 points can teach the onset head to leave the floor without inflating V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the onset-floor error confined to a structural subregion, or does it occur whenever retention is predicted near zero?

feedback_interpretation: Recent labels strengthened the separation between onset and tail repair. The m198 2/1 result 6f43332e2665523bcccc overpredicted V2 while the 5/1 and 50/1 points 5a279bc25d91d033acdc and 0ac58929e586a4da4056 were much closer, so the batch emphasizes local loading and ratio contrasts rather than a global correction. The m177 lower-loading 50/1 result 4862e2fb71344ce16021 had a short measured tail despite a very broad prediction, confirming that quantile width is not reliable uncertainty. The m141 result 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 still underpredicted V1 while V2 was close, and the m178 results 17ff889395addf7d6295 and 855456da9ea892f7216b show opposite V1/V2 failure patterns. The m205, m216, m90, and m193 outcomes also support loading-dependent response surfaces. These observations motivate paired local curves, direct V2 calibration points, and low-similarity transfer anchors.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs several known failure regions while preserving structural coverage. m177, m178, and m198 provide intermediate points around onset floors, steep transitions, and anomalous V2 tails. m141, m204, m205, m216, m90, m193, m212, m163, and m146 add matched loading or ratio contrasts so retraining can separate mobile-phase effects from loading effects and learn how V1 and V2 respond differently. m203 and m104 target late-regime overprediction, while four low-similarity molecule-novel rows cover bulky aryl ketone, brominated alcohol, multifunctional carbonyl, and phosphoryl environments. Together these labels supervise local response surfaces, tail calibration, output decoupling, and transfer into underrepresented structural regions, which should improve generalization across the Row-distribution.
